editorialSource.formula: Contribution per unit = selling price − variable cost. Exact units = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit (or zero when fixed costs are zero). Whole units = ceiling(exact units). Break-even revenue = whole units × selling price.
steps: Enter fixed costs, selling price per unit and variable cost per unit.
Subtract variable cost from selling price to calculate contribution.
Divide fixed costs by contribution to get exact break-even volume.
Round units up to the next whole number.
Multiply whole units by selling price to estimate break-even revenue and calculate total costs.
assumptions: Selling price, variable cost and fixed costs are assumed constant.
Whole units are rounded up because fractional units are not treated as sellable.
Product mix, capacity, tax, financing and changing costs/prices are excluded.

faqs.question: What is contribution per unit?
faqs.answer: Selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit.

faqs.question: Why round units up?
faqs.answer: A business generally cannot sell a fraction of a unit, so the practical target rounds up.

faqs.question: Are taxes included?
faqs.answer: No. Financing, tax, product mix and capacity constraints are excluded.
